newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell, Millennium set olefins, polymers venture.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell, Millennium set olefins, polymers venture.

text.p: Lyondell Petrochemical Co and Millennium Chemicals Inc said Monday they signed a definitive agreement to form a venture comprised primarily of their olefins and polymers businesses.
Lyondell Petrochemical will own 57 percent of the new company, Millennium 43 percent. To be operated as a partnership, it is expected to have annual revenues of $5 billion.
The venture will be governed by a six-person committee co-chaired by Dan Smith, chief executive of Lyondell, and William Landuyt, chief executive of Millennium.
Smith also will serve as chief executive of the venture, which will be headquartered in Houston, Texas.

The companies said the combination will have book assets of about $5 billion. It plans to have $1.745 billion of debt, with a note receivable from Lyondell of $345 million, and substantial free cash flow.

They said the new company will consist of 13 manufacturing facilities on the U.S. Gulf Coast and in the U.S. Midwest, producing ethylene, propylene, polyethylene, polypropylene, ethyl alcohol and associated products.
The companies expect the partnership to generate more than $150 million in annual pre-tax profit improvement.
They said they expect to see "substantial" savings early, with the full $150 million annual savings achieved by the end of 1999.
The companies said they expect to close the deal by the end of the year.
